item.title: Midterm Blue Wave Triggers Political Backlash Against AI and Data Centers
item.description:
Midterm Blue Wave Triggers Political Backlash Against AI and Data Centers

On Tuesday night voters delivered a historic Democratic sweep—taking control of the House and Senate, electing the nation’s first Black woman governor in Georgia, the first Native American woman governor in New Mexico, and flipping a long‑standing Maine Senate seat. The outcome introduced a new political front against artificial‑intelligence companies, centering on regulation and data‑center construction.

🔍 Overview

  • Democrats achieved a “blue wave” that swept traditionally red and swing states.
  • The election produced the first Black woman governor (Georgia) and the first Native American woman governor (New Mexico).
  • A Maine Senator, in office for 30 years, ceded to a Democrat.
  • The results were described as a “total repudiation” of the AI field by Wes McEnany of the Future of Life Institute.

⚖️ Policy Backlash

  • Campaigns emphasized “holding AI companies accountable to the American people.”
  • Incoming leaders have pledged to drag AI CEOs to testify.
  • The backlash against data‑center construction is cited as the most tangible manifestation of that sentiment.
  • The Guardrails Alliance calls the data‑center issue “one of the most bipartisan political issues” they’ve seen.
  • The Tech Oversight Project links data‑center opposition to broader corporate‑accountability concerns.

🏗️ Data‑Center Moratoria

  • 43 of 44 local data‑center moratoria on Tuesday’s ballots passed.
  • In Texas, governor‑elect Gina Hinojosa plans to issue a moratorium on all data‑center approvals until protective legislation is passed.
  • Similar moratorium promises have been made in a handful of other key states.
  • NBC News polling shows 76 percent of voters oppose data centers in their communities.
  • Meta’s platforms president, Dina Powell McCormick, says many are considering moving data‑center construction abroad.

💬 Industry Reaction

  • Publicly, most major AI CEOs have remained silent; OpenAI and Anthropic did not comment to The Verge, and Elon Musk’s X post vanished after the results.
  • Privately, CEOs—including OpenAI’s—have discussed significant compute‑capacity constraints following the election, per the Wall Street Journal.
  • OpenAI recently began calling its data centers “compute campuses.”
  • Analysts note the results likely ended Republican attempts to block state‑level AI restrictions, with some saying any member voting to wipe out those laws faces electoral risk.

📈 Outlook

  • Experts expect a rise in “tech accountability bills” and more questions about who benefits from AI infrastructure.
  • While Trump’s September effort to rename AI as “super intelligence” and corporate re‑branding continue, midterm results indicate many voters are not buying the narrative.
  • The political environment suggests a tougher path for AI companies to expand compute campuses across the United States.

#AIRegulation #DataCenters #Midterms #PoliticalBacklash

Source: ‘Total repudiation’: The blue wave is about to hit AI

item.title: Trump Signs Executive Order Replacing AI Terminology with Super Intelligence
item.description:
Trump Signs Executive Order Replacing AI Terminology with Super Intelligence

President Donald Trump has signed an executive order directing the US executive branch to stop acknowledging the existence of “artificial intelligence” and instead use the term “Super Intelligence.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Scope of Change: Official policy websites, press releases, and policy documents will now refer only to “Super Intelligence.”
  • Usage Requirements: US officials are expected to not acknowledge the use of “AI” or “artificial intelligence” in relevant settings.
  • Regulatory Status: Executive agencies are not required to change past documents or regulations.
  • Terminology: While “superintelligence” is an industry term for powerful versions of AI, the administration is using it as a replacement for the broader statutory definition of AI.

💡 Why it matters

President Trump stated the rebrand aims to quell fears regarding safety risks and the speed of AI advancement. Regarding the terminology, he noted:

  • “The word super is the best word of all, and it’s the simplest”
  • “We don’t want to hear artificial. Because it’s not artificial. It’s very powerful, it’s very brilliant.”
  • He compared the word “artificial” to “fake news.”

🔍 Overview

The order follows a White House luncheon with government officials and tech CEOs, including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. During these discussions, the following points were addressed:

  • Regulation: Trump mentioned a belief in “tremendous self-regulation” and noted existing regulation through the FBI and Department of Justice.
  • Infrastructure: To address local hurdles in building massive data centers, Trump stated firms will “work to make the community happy” via economic support and resources, adding that “data centers are going to be very popular.”
  • Usage: Trump stated the technology “is going to mostly be put to good use and we’ll stop the bad use.”

#SuperIntelligence #ExecutiveOrder #USGovernment #TechPolicy

Source: Trump orders US government to call AI ‘Super Intelligence’

item.title: California Governor Signs Laws Regulating AI Data Center Energy and Water Use
item.description:
California Governor Signs Laws Regulating AI Data Center Energy and Water Use

California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed a package of seven bills designed to regulate the utility consumption of AI data centers and prevent them from passing costs onto residents.

⚙️ Key details

The new legislation mandates several operational requirements for data centers:

Requirement Description
Rate Classification The California Public Utilities Commission must introduce a new rate classification for data centers.
Infrastructure Costs Data centers are required to pay for upgrades to local power grids and water systems.
Transparency Proposed data centers must disclose estimated water use, energy efficiency, and drought planning to local governments.
Approval Process Facilities must meet specific energy, water, and fuel consumption requirements to qualify for a streamlined approval process.

💡 Why it matters

Governor Newsom stated that these laws aim to ensure that those profiting from data centers do not do so at the expense of residents. He noted that the regulations address community concerns regarding electricity demand, grid constraints, water use, and pollution. Additionally, the Governor signed a separate executive order last week to accelerate the creation of an AI “kill switch.”

#California #AI #DataCenters #EnergyPolicy #Regulation

Source: California tightens rules on AI data center energy and water use

item.title: Trump Asserts Federal Oversight Authority and Opposes Restrictive AI Guardrails
item.description:
Trump Asserts Federal Oversight Authority and Opposes Restrictive AI Guardrails

US President Donald Trump stated Monday that his administration holds extensive oversight and regulatory power over artificial intelligence companies, rejecting calls for restrictive guardrails as a conspiracy benefiting Beijing. The president vowed to maintain American dominance in the sector, arguing that domestic debates over slowing AI expansion only satisfy Chinese interests.

⚙️ Key details

  • President Trump asserted on his Truth Social platform that the federal government maintains “sweeping oversight authority” and “tremendous criminal and regulatory power” over tech enterprises.
  • The president specifically singled out Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei for “pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’” regarding industry safety debates.
  • US Vice President JD Vance characterized corporate lobbying for state restrictions as a potential “Trojan horse,” suggesting that frontier AI tech companies are begging for regulation for disingenuous reasons.
  • Trump warned against domestic policies that would “kill the Golden Goose,” claiming the U.S. currently leads all other countries by a significant margin.

🔍 Overview

Stakeholder Role / Organization Stated Position or Action
Donald Trump US President Asserts that a “strong and smart” president is the only necessary control for AI.
JD Vance US Vice President Advocates for “smart” regulation while warning against disingenuous corporate lobbying.
Dario Amodei CEO of Anthropic Proposed that firms deliberately slow capability growth to ensure safety protocols keep pace.
Sam Altman CEO of OpenAI Confirmed that his company would adopt measures similar to Amodei’s safety proposal.
Guo Jiakun Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Urged an “open, inclusive and universally beneficial” environment and rejected “fear-mongering.”

💡 Why it matters

  • Global Competition: President Trump affirmed that the US leads global competitors and must maintain dominance because “whoever wins AI, wins!”
  • Industry Safety Debate: The administration’s stance coincides with a push from industry leaders like Dario Amodei and Sam Altman to moderate the speed of model deployment to ensure safety.
  • International Friction: The US administration views restrictive domestic guardrails as a benefit to China, while China has warned that such framing creates “malicious competition” damaging to global governance.
  • Regulatory Approach: While the president focuses on executive strength as a guardrail, Vice President Vance stressed that Washington must be thoughtful about risks while maintaining its advantage against China.

#AIRegulation #NationalSecurity #Anthropic #OpenAI #TechPolicy

Source: Trump warns AI critics serve China, claims US regulatory power
